key_insight: Generalized hydrodynamic stability analysis reveals rarefaction-driven changes in high-speed plane Couette flow that classical Navier–Stokes theory misses, with all modes becoming stable as rarefaction increases.
engineering_relevance: The method supports stability assessment of high-altitude shear flows where slip and nonequilibrium transport make continuum predictions less reliable.
method: Develop temporal linear stability analysis using 13-moment generalized hydrodynamic equations with slip boundaries.
Compare with nonlinear coupled constitutive relations and Navier–Stokes stability formulations.
Analyze base flows, eigenspectra and mode synchronization across Mach and Knudsen numbers.
evidence_signal: For Ma = 2.5–10 and Kn = 2.7×10⁻⁵–0.07, GHE base-flow predictions agree well with DSMC, while GHE and Navier–Stokes stability predictions differ considerably at Kn ~ 0.01.
watch_item: The abstract reports DSMC agreement for base flows, not direct validation of disturbance growth rates; conclusions concern temporal linear stability of plane Couette flow.
paper_title: A linear stability method based on generalized hydrodynamics: application to high-speed plane Couette flow beyond continuum regime
